items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'Plot twist' / 'Twist ये है' gets a playful, knowing, excited lift. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. The 1981 royal-wedding coup story is told like a thrilling, almost unbelievable spy story. Gambia's reply is a cheeky, proud little voice-wink. The last line trails off unfinished, voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Pronounce Senegal as SEN-ih-gawl, Gambia as GAM-bee-uh, Senegambia as sen-ih-GAM-bee-uh, Dakar as DAH-kar and Banjul as BAN-jool.
lines: What if Senegal and The Gambia became one country?
Four hundred eighty kilometers long... but only forty-eight kilometers wide.
The story goes, British cannonballs drew this border.
Not quite... it's ten kilometers each side of the river.
So what would this country get?
Twenty million people... one coastline... and the whole Gambia River.
And no border posts between north Senegal and the south.
But that's not even the weirdest part.
In nineteen eighty-one, Gambia's president flew to London...
...for the royal wedding of Charles and Diana.
And back home, rebels tried a coup!
Senegal sent twenty-seven hundred troops and saved him.
It lasted seven years... then split over who'd be president.
And the capital? Huge Dakar... or tiny Banjul?
Gambia's reply? We're small... but the river's ours.
So... one country, or two? Because honestly...
